title: Count Words Without split()'s Empty-String Surprise
statement:
`String.split` is the obvious tool for "break this into words" -- and it
has one behaviour that catches almost everyone once: splitting an empty
string does not give you an empty array. `Scanner`, tokenising the same
string the way it would tokenise real input, does not have this problem
at all.

## Your function

```
public static int countWords(String text);
```

Return how many whitespace-separated words `text` contains. Words may be
separated by any run of spaces or tabs, of any length; leading and
trailing whitespace do not count as words. `text` may be empty.

## Watch out

- **`"".split("\\s+")` returns an array of length `1`, not `0`.** Its
  single element is the empty string -- `split` never produces zero
  pieces, because "the whole input, unsplit" is still one piece even when
  that piece is empty. `countWords("")` computed as
  `text.split("\\s+").length` comes back `1`, not the `0` this function's
  contract asks for.
- **A string that is entirely whitespace has the identical problem**,
  for the identical reason: trimming it first gives you `""`, and
  splitting *that* still returns one empty-string element, not zero.
- **`new Scanner(text)` sidesteps the whole issue.** Its `hasNext()` /
  `next()` pair only ever produces genuine, non-empty tokens -- an empty
  or all-whitespace `text` simply has no tokens to produce, and
  `hasNext()` reports `false` immediately, with no special case needed
  for either.

tests.name: an empty line has no words
tests.description: text.split("\\s+").length on an empty string is 1, not 0 -- this is the case that catches that.

tests.name: runs of multiple spaces between words
tests.description: Three separators, each more than one space wide -- still three words, not more.

tests.name: leading and trailing whitespace do not add words
a line that is whitespace only has no words
